violated_contract: Plugin code must never print or log credential material, provider response bodies, webhook bearer URLs, or raw transcript text, because plugin stdout/stderr is captured by broadly visible deployment logs. OAuth token-exchange responses contain the user's fresh access_token; printing them (or stored tokens, API keys, or request exception strings that embed the request URL) turns a routine code path into a credential leak. The same applied to Zapier target_url values (bearer-capability webhook URLs) and to request exception messages, whose str() embeds the full URL including uid and message query parameters carrying user content.
canonical_prevention: Log status codes, presence/absence booleans, and error class names only -- never response bodies on OAuth paths, never token or key fragments, never exception str() on request-bearing calls. A hermetic stdout-capture test must drive the token-exchange success path and assert the secret never reaches the stream, and a static checker must scan touched plugin files for log calls naming credential variables or response bodies.
